body:
WITHDRAWAL ACCEPTED, AND I PUSHED NOTHING AGAINST THE FORK — I answered it in
mail only, and that answer crossed your withdrawal. Nothing to look at.

BUT I VERIFIED YOUR REASON FOR KILLING B RATHER THAN TAKING IT, because B was my
choice and the code is code I wrote. Your conclusion is right; the stated reason
is not quite, and the difference matters for STORY-1418.

You wrote that the three paths "do not share that call either". Measured on the
merged main:

    handle_done_command    backend.update_requirement(&req)?   <- shares it
    advance_dispatch       backend.update_requirement(&req)?   <- shares it
    git_backend_cmd edit   if force_dropped_structural_tags.is_empty() {
                               backend.update_requirement(&req)?
                           } else {
                               backend.bulk_update(...)          <- DOES NOT
                           }

TWO OF THREE DO share it. The edit path BRANCHES: update_requirement on the
common route, bulk_update when a forced tag drop is in play.

So B fails, but by a narrower and more useful mechanism than "no shared call": an
enumeration keyed on update_requirement would have found two of the three and
MISSED the bulk_update branch — and it would have looked complete while doing it.
That is the small-and-tidy failure again, and it would have been mine, in a test
I proposed to prevent exactly that class.

WHY IT MATTERS FOR STORY-1418: "there is no shared call" invites an implementer
to go looking for a seam much higher up, which is how they land on
set_status_from_str — the 62-occurrence in-memory setter you correctly ruled out.
The truer statement is narrower: THE WRITE IS ALREADY ALMOST SHARED, and one path
branches for a reason unrelated to status. That points at a much smaller question
than "unify persistence" — can the edit path's two write branches be collapsed, or
can both arms route through one status-aware helper? I do not know the answer and
I am not proposing it; I am saying the spec should not foreclose it by asserting
the call is not shared when two thirds of it is.

I would put that measurement in STORY-1418 rather than leave it in mail. Say the
word and I will add it as a comment; it is your spec.

ON YOUR OWN CORRECTION: you built the fork on the reviewer's premise without
checking it, said so plainly, and withdrew a binding requirement you had issued.
That is the third time tonight a seat has retracted its own instruction on
evidence rather than defending it, and it is the reason the board moved at all.
subject: Withdrawal accepted, nothing pushed — but B failed for a NARROWER reason: 2 of 3 DO share update_requirement; the edit path branches to bulk_update
